cards.title: Security sweep: patched dependencies, unsafe loading fixed, dead web API removed
cards.plain: All 82 open advisories (5 critical, 43 high) are fixed by upgrading 7 packages, and the code no longer loads untrusted pickles or checkpoints unsafely.
cards.chosen: Pillow 13.0.0, torch 2.14.1 / torchvision 0.29.1, transformers 5.21.1, diffusers 0.42.1, accelerate 1.15.0, datasets 5.1.0, requests 2.34.2 (each release at least two weeks old, 0 OSV advisories across all 144 resolved packages). `torch.load` always uses `weights_only=True`; pickles go through a restricted loader; `trust_remote_code` removed. The unauthenticated FastAPI/Gradio code in `videox_fun/api` and `videox_fun/ui` was deleted: it was not importable (missing `controller` module), and it let any caller load any model path, fetch any URL and read any file. The notebook now clones this repo instead of upstream's vulnerable pins. Details: `docs/SECURITY.md`.
cards.why: Security rows are due 2 days (critical) and 7 days (high) from first sight (SPEC §6.1). Removing broken, unreachable network code is safer than hardening it.
cards.if_ignored: Nothing to do: confirm, or overturn if you want a demo UI back (it would be rebuilt with a login and the self-check page).

cards.title: The Streamlit review tool was assessed against the Security Self-Check standard
cards.plain: void-model has no hosted web front end. Its one web page, a local review tool, was assessed in full.
cards.chosen: `conformance/void-model.toml` in `security-self-check` covers the Streamlit physics review tool in `data_generation/`, from the code and a live run on 2026-11-13: 12 yes, 9 no, 84 n/a. It listens on 127.0.0.1 only. Other web sites cannot rebind it or open its WebSocket (403 on both, `server.allowedHosts` and the Origin check). It leaks no version and no file. The 9 no rows are the security headers Streamlit cannot send (CSP, frame protection, nosniff and four more) and the lack of a sign-in; D-01 asks what to do about them.
cards.why: The standard covers every web front end (STANDARD.md §1.1). Assessing the one page is more honest than calling the repo out of scope.
cards.if_ignored: Nothing to do: confirm, or overturn with a note.

cards.title: Streamlit review tool: accept the missing headers and sign-in, or do more?
cards.plain: The local review tool cannot send security headers and has no sign-in. Other web sites are already blocked from it.
cards.why: Self-check rows hdr-csp, hdr-framing, hdr-nosniff, hdr-referrer, hdr-permissions, hdr-coop, hdr-corp and auth-api-gated are **no** in `conformance/void-model.toml` (see X-02). The tool runs only on the machine where someone starts it, for curating synthetic training data.

options.text: Accept as is: loopback only, no sign-in, no self-check page. Re-assess in 90 days or if the tool is ever hosted.
Put a small local reverse proxy in front of it that adds the headers. It adds a moving part for one user.
Retire the web tool. The physics config is edited by hand or with a command-line script instead.

cards.if_ignored: Option a stays in force: the tool keeps working as now, on loopback.

phases.label: Fixed: kubric 0.1.1 in data_generation/requirements-kubric.txt until 2027-02-11
phases.note: Gone from the report on 2026-11-13. no release since 2021-08-25 (newest 0.1.1), over 3 years. Accepted until 2027-02-11: kubric 0.1.1 (PyPI, 2021) has no OSV advisory (checked 2026-11-13). It runs only in the optional offline synthetic-data generator (data_generation/kubric_variable_objects.py), never in inference or training. Upstream ships Kubric as its Docker image (kubricdockerhub/kubruntu) rather than PyPI releases; moving the generator to that image pinned by digest is tracked on the void-model BUILD board.

phases.note: Gone from the report on 2026-11-13. no release since 2021-06-14 (newest 0.6.0), over 3 years. It reads training videos only (videox_fun/data/dataset_*.py and the MPS reward), never at inference. Replacing it with a maintained decoder (torchcodec or PyAV) changes the training data path and needs a GPU training check: tracked on the void-model BUILD board.

about.what: An offline, ARM64-ready edition of Netflix's VOID model: removes objects from videos together with the physical effects they cause (shadows, falls, collisions), built on CogVideoX.
about.why: The upstream VOID release depends on cloud APIs and x86 binaries. This edition runs fully offline on DGX Spark (ARM64, Ubuntu 24.04), with a local Gemma model for mask reasoning and a prebuilt decord wheel, so video inpainting can run without sending footage to a third party.
about.who: chappa.ai and researchers who run video object removal and its training or synthetic-data pipelines on their own GPU hosts, especially DGX Spark.
